purpose: determine whether an authentic per-segment Protocol-A score artifact, created during the original locked test run, still exists anywhere
rule_applied: recovering an existing artifact is permitted; generating one is not

locations_searched.result: 4 files matched, all aggregate-only: evaluate_RoboticArm.json, evaluate_BrushlessMotor.json, protocol_a_primary_auc.csv, protocol_a_reproduction_report.json. None contains a per-segment row.

locations_searched.method: full file listing plus HDF5 dataset enumeration
locations_searched.result: 6 files only: 2 checkpoints and 4 windowed HDF5 datasets. The HDF5 files contain exactly the 3 sensor arrays and 5 label arrays written at preprocessing time; no score dataset was ever added.
synopsis rendering assets and scripts only; no Protocol-A score data.

locations_searched.result: matches are source code only (the artifact generator scripts and the pinned upstream notebooks). locations_searched.result: no per-segment score artifact was ever committed and later removed.

locations_searched.method: git stash list; git fsck --lost-found; inspected every dangling blob

nothing beside the checkpoints except the windowed HDF5 inputs.

root_cause: scripts/run_protocol_a_reproduction.py stage_evaluate builds the grouped per-segment score table in memory and returns only the aggregate AUC dictionary. The table is never written to disk.
permanent_record: Per-segment Protocol-A scores were not persisted during the original locked test run and cannot be reconstructed without re-inference.
why_not_resolved: Resolution requires the original score values. They do not exist. Re-running inference with the frozen checkpoint would produce new values, not recovered ones, and would constitute a new test access requiring separate authorisation and versioning. That was not done.
why_not_red: Nothing indicates the recorded aggregates are wrong. The AUC estimator was independently validated against upstream's brute-force nested loop, all 42 primary_auc.csv rows are exactly consistent with the evaluator output, both test cohort hashes recompute correctly, and the evaluator provably loaded the trained checkpoints. What is missing is re-derivability, not correctness.
future_option_not_exercised_here: A deliberate re-inference against the same frozen checkpoint could create a reproducibility artifact, but it would be a NEW test access and must be separately authorised and versioned.
